title: Stable Matching on the Job? Theory and Evidence on Internal Talent Markets
eligible_reason: No difference-in-differences or event-study design. The empirical tables (Tables 3-8) are summary statistics, average match-quality scores by matching algorithm from simulations, and cross-sectional regressions of worker/manager rankings on standardized firm-objective scores (reg worker`var' fos_std, cluster(workerid_new); reghdfe workernum1 totalgrowth_std ... absorb(workerid_new managerid_new)). No binary treatment switching on over time.
design_notes: Worker-manager preference data from one firm's internal talent market (confidential; replaced by a simulated dataset). R scripts simulate preferences and run deferred-acceptance / Hungarian / random assignments; Stata scripts tabulate match quality and regress rankings on scores. 'ft_staggered' flag is a false positive.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: No staggered binary adoption in the reported designs.
data_files_note: README: the paper's data are private; the package is meant to ship a simulated wrkr-mgr-fixed-preferences.csv, but the Data folder in the extracted package is empty (only .DS_Store); Simulate-Preferences.R can regenerate simulated preferences.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (README PDF). Not a DiD paper.
